 Crl.P No. 4535 of 2024
 Order

The petitioners- accused Nos.1 and 3 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.62 of 2024, Shanivarasanthe Police Station, pending on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Somavarapete, Kodagu registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 r/w Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant- Smt. Sadhana.
2. Heard Sri Abhishek Huddar, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri K.P.Yashodha, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioners are entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"
NC: 2024:KHC:20492

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioners being accused Nos.1 and 3 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail on the apprehension of being arrested.
The deceased personally lodged the first information after consuming poison, making allegation against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 504 of IPC.
Later, Section 306 of IPC was also invoked.
It is alleged that petitioner No.1 used to treat the deceased with cruelty.
Admittedly, he was working at Assam and he was not present in the house when the incident had occurred.
It is not in dispute that accused No.2 is already granted anticipatory bail.
As per the first information, the only allegation against accused No.3 is that he abused the deceased to leave the matrimonial home along with clothes and she need not have to return back.
It is thereafter, she consumed poison.
Later, she died on 08.04.2024.
I do not find any reason to reject the claim of the petitioners for anticipatory bail.
The interest of the prosecution could be safeguarded by imposing NC: 2024:KHC:20492 suitable conditions.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioners may be granted anticipatory bail subject to conditions.

5. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
